account: Today I inspected the mill, attended tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage, and returned to the office. The mill stall held seventy-seven hay bales, and I crossed the bridge without trouble. There are rumours about changes to the bridge or port, but the neighbour has witnessed none and knows nothing definite; I have no evidence confirming them. The neighbour also reported that the baker said the market was well stocked this morning. The scheduled council correspondence did not materialise: the secretary found appointment books in the office chest but no council letters, and reported no delivery known to the baker. I asked her to stop searching and record that none were found, rather than assume something had happened to them. The unusual business this evening is the approved eighteen hundred great-hall lighting and table inspection involving the builder, with Freight also mentioned in preparation inquiries. Neither the secretary nor the neighbour has a fresh confirmation that preparations are ready. I heard the builder speaking earlier but could not make out the words, so cannot attribute any explanation to them. My direct route into the hall was blocked; that alone does not establish why. I have stepped through the open office doorway and agreed with the neighbour to wait until eighteen, since she says we were asked not to disturb preparations beforehand. It is now seventeen fifty-seven. I understand the gathering to be a lighting and table inspection, but do not yet know what has actually been prepared or whether there is any further purpose.
